You can report suspected substandard or falsified medicines to NAFDAC using the following channels:

* Report to your nearest NAFDAC office [1].
* Call NAFDAC on **0800-1-NAFDAC (1800-1-623322)** [1] or **0800-162-3322** [2].
* Send an email to **sf.alert@nafdac.gov.ng** [2].
* Report side effects or adverse events via the Med-safety mobile application (available on Android and iOS) or by email to **pharmacovigilance@nafdac.gov.ng** [2].

Yes. According to NAFDAC Public Alert No. 027/2025, batch T36184B of Postinor 2 is a confirmed counterfeit (Type 1) product that was not imported by the marketing authorization holder [1]. 

The alert notes that the falsified pack may feature the spelling error **"Veify"** instead of "Verify" on the pin sticker and **"Distnibuted"** instead of "distributed" on the back [1]. 

If you have this batch, do not use it. You can report it to NAFDAC by calling **0800-162-3322** or emailing **sf.alert@nafdac.gov.ng** [1]. Consult a pharmacist if you are in doubt [1].

The scratch code is part of NAFDAC's Mobile Authentication Service (MAS) scheme to help consumers detect substandard and falsified medicines at the point of purchase [1]. 

* You scratch the panel on the pack to reveal a unique, one-time use PIN [1].
* You send this PIN via SMS (toll-free) to the short code printed on the pack [1].
* You receive a text message response stating whether the product is genuine or suspected fake [1].

- At least 1 in 10 medicines in low- and middle-income countries are substandard or falsified [2].
- Low- and middle-income countries, as well as areas of conflict or civil unrest with very weak or non-existent health systems, bear the greatest burden of these products [1].
- Countries spend an estimated US$ 30.5 billion per year on substandard and falsified medical products [2].
